resolution_caveats.noIndexArm: THE ARM IS INDEX=NO AND THAT IS THE HONEST ARM: there is no INDEX_SPECS entry for kotlin in script/m14/incoming-gate.ts, so no production project index is built. TABLE 1's scope is the gate's own per-repository declaration table, built from every file the RUN parsed — and the arm is three SLICE runs, so each slice resolves against its own slice-scoped table (2346 admitted over 8 repositories in the union).
resolution_caveats.sliceScopeResolution: ★ THE CLOSURE IS THE SUM OF THREE SLICE RUNS, AND PER-PROJECT RESOLUTION IS NOT ADDITIVE ACROSS SLICES — MEASURED, STATED, NOT HIDDEN: a single whole-population run of the SAME gate over the SAME 2346 files (validation/m14/measurements/kotlin-gate-whole-2026-10-25.txt) reads edges 257,582 (IDENTICAL) but resolved 100,228 (+1,893 vs the closure), amb(decl) 75,735 (+9,257), unresolved 70,742 (−11,137), extOK 10,855 (−13). The difference is the per-project declaration table's COMPLETENESS — a property of the run's SCOPE, not of the analyzer: a slice resolves against the declarations of the files in THAT slice, so a name whose other declaration lies outside the slice can read unresolved where the whole run reads ambiguous. The slice-merged closure is the fleet's arm protocol (3 contiguous slices over [0, 2346)) and is the declared measurement; the whole-run reading is published beside it so no reader assumes the two agree.
resolution_caveats.collResSubset: `collRes` (25311) is a SUBSET of resolved — a resolved edge whose target has MORE THAN ONE declaration in the project, so the tie-break chose the row. NEVER added to `resolved`. The fleet's own indexer measures 37,318 of 49,729 such picks as WRONG, so the resolved column is a FLOOR on correctness, not a count of correct edges; the per-row number is published so a reader can discount it.
resolution_caveats.ambKindSubset: `amb(kind)` (33194) is a SUBSET of `amb(decl)` (66478): distinct KINDS among colliding declarations vs distinct DECLARATIONS. Reported beside it, never added; only amb(decl) is in the closure.
